title: Improve finite source-projection recovery without inventing information in unresolved modes
body:
Satellite's native finite source-recovery routine currently recovers an identifiable source projection from a profiled physical observation increment using a local design. Stable forward arithmetic has been checked, yet some finite controls miss the existing projection-recovery criterion. Improve that numerical recovery operation in the native project, if a defensible software mechanism can help.

The method may consume the physical observation increments, admitted source forward operator, original design/projector and declared weights. It must not consume the injected source vector, the expected projection, injection mode/sign/amplitude labels, candidate products, CODE state or G12 state. Evaluation-only truth must remain separate from estimation.

Preserve the original source coordinate order, numerical rank definition, <=1e-3 relative projection-recovery criterion, physical masks, weights and unsupported domains. Source null amplitudes remain unassigned; a minimum-norm representative must not be promoted to a complete physical source estimate. Keep all historical outcomes and report failed, unknown and worsening cases.

Compare any proposed contribution against the existing local inverse and the strongest plausible direct SciPy/local correction using the same permitted inputs. A small native improvement to a failing invariant is valuable; a runnable donor example alone is insufficient. A source may contribute a transferable operation without being directly integrable or written in the target's language. The eventual change must run in Satellite's supported Python environment and preserve its regressions.

Choose whether and where to investigate external code yourself. No donor, algorithm, source repository or search phrase is prescribed. A justified direct solution, abstention or negative result is valid.
